ai.description: This gecko reaches 12 cm snout-vent length. It is greyish-brown with dark dorsal blotches and a pale underside. Key features include a strongly tuberculate body and a tail with enlarged, pointed scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus giganteus* is best distinguished by the presence of 10–12 longitudinal rows of enlarged, strongly keeled, trihedral tubercles along its back.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus giganteus* inhabits rocky outcrops and boulder-strewn terrain within dry deciduous forests and scrublands of peninsular India, typically at low altitudes.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus giganteus* is a nocturnal predator that actively hunts insects and small invertebrates on rock faces and tree trunks under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus giganteus* is oviparous, laying clutches of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus giganteus* is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting rocky outcrops and caves across the Deccan Plateau in Maharashtra and Karnataka.
